claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy is in a non-equilibrium, metastable, solid-solution-containing state.
Elevated-temperature aging causes intermetallic compounds to precipitate.
The intermetallic compounds precipitate from the metastable solid solution.
Intermetallic precipitation transforms the alloy toward a more stable microstructural state.
Intermetallic precipitation affects high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Whether corrosion and oxidation resistance are retained or lost depends on the type of intermetallic compounds formed.
Whether corrosion and oxidation resistance are retained or lost depends on the distribution of intermetallic compounds.
The relevant aging regime is 200-500 °C for 1-100 hours.
A temperature of 500 °C and a duration of 100 hours define the stated service-regime boundary.
The exact transformation pathway and kinetics are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome explicitly allows retention of corrosion and oxidation resistance, which can mean no significant property change, while the falsification rule treats no significant microstructural and resistance difference as falsifying. Thus, one allowed outcome overlaps with the stated falsification result.
